record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Large-data defocusing NLS without localized states
record.original_question: For a time-independent positive localized potential V(x), can one prove for large data that the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation i∂tψ = -∆ψ + V(x)ψ + |ψ(x,t)|²ψ has no localized solutions? Small-data cases are known from Lp estimates for the linear part, but the open case concerns large bounded solutions that are known only to converge to a free wave plus a weakly localized component in dimensions three and higher.

evidence.quote: A simplified version of this problem is as follows: prove that the equation below has no localized solutions for a time-independent V that is positive as described. For small data, this is known, utilizing the Lp estimates for the linear part. Our analysis demonstrates that for large data, all bounded solutions of this equation converge to a free wave plus a weakly localized solution in three or more dimensions. It’s noteworthy that the nonlinear term is defocusing. i∂ψ ∂t = − ∆ψ +V (x)ψ + |ψ (x,t )|2ψ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ ($d\geq 3$) be a time-independent, smooth, positive, spatially localized potential (e.g. compactly supported and strictly positive on its support, or more generally rapidly decaying at infinity with $V(x)>0$). Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi(x,t) \;=\; -\Delta \psi(x,t) \;+\; V(x)\,\psi(x,t) \;+\; |\psi(x,t)|^{2}\,\psi(x,t), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}, $$
with initial data $\psi(\cdot,0)\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ of arbitrary (large) size. A nontrivial global solution $\psi$ is called localized if there exists a sequence of times $t_n\to\infty$ and a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ such that
$$ \liminf_{n\to\infty} \int_{K} |\psi(x,t_n)|^2\,dx \;>\; 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sup_{t\geq 0}\|\psi(\cdot,t)\|_{H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty, $$
i.e. a nontrivial portion of the mass remains concentrated in a bounded region for all time.

Prove (or disprove) that for every such positive localized potential $V$ and for arbitrarily large $H^1$ initial data, the equation above admits no nontrivial localized solutions: every bounded global solution scatters to a free linear wave as $t\to\pm\infty$.

(The small-data version of this statement is known via $L^p$ estimates for the linear part. It is also known that any bounded global solution decomposes asymptotically into a free wave plus a weakly localized component; the question is whether the weakly localized component must vanish.)
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g. on scattering and localized states for defocusing NLS with potential, 2024) establish a decomposition of bounded global solutions into a free wave plus a weakly localized component in dimensions ≥ 3, but ruling out the weakly localized part for arbitrary large data with a positive localized potential remains an open problem highlighted in current reviews of nonlinear scattering theory.

status_evidence.title: Scattering and localized states for defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equations with potential
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions decompose into a free wave and a weakly localized part which is asymptotically orthogonal to any fixed free wave.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art establishes free-wave + weakly localized decomposition, but does not rule out the weakly localized component.

status_evidence.title: A new paradigm for scattering theory of linear and nonlinear waves: review and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Prove that the equation has no localized solutions for a time-independent positive V; for small data this is known, the open case concerns large data.
status_evidence.claim: The large-data nonexistence of localized solutions is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The asymptotic behaviour of large data solutions to NLS
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of asymptotic behaviour and weakly bound states for NLS with potential.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the conjecture that no nontrivial weakly bound states exist for defocusing NLS with positive potential.
